subject: Network shielding and connectivity summary for SOC2 evidence
messages:
From: Linda Hayes <linda.hayes@openbank.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: short network summary + evidence for SOC2 review

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. As part of our SOC2 readiness checklist we need a concise architecture summary that explains how Redwood isolates Dedicated/Private deployments from the public internet and from the control plane, plus your egress and failover behavior. Specifically we need: 

- A one-page diagram that shows network boundaries for Dedicated and Private (VPC peering, NAT/eBGP, edge components).
- A short table/matrix that maps traffic flows (control plane, model fetch, monitoring, telemetry, customer inference traffic) to interfaces and ACLs.
- Notes on KV/cache persistence and whether any inference cache is ever egressed to Redwood-managed public endpoints.
- How failover between regions or Dedicated pools works (if primary pool is unavailable).

Goal is a single packet we can attach to the SOC2 evidence folder. PDF or Drive link is fine. Can you share by end of day PT?

Thanks,
Linda Hayes
Security Engineer, OpenBank

--
OpenBank Security Team
security@openbank.com

Team — forwarding OpenBank's ask below. They want a compact artifact for SOC2: diagram + traffic matrix + short failover note. Naomi goal: ship a 1-page and an XLS mapping.

Key constraints from the call: Dedicated must show network boundary at the GPU pool level, private deployments show customer VPC + optional air-gap pattern. Control plane traffic must be labeled and evidence that control plane management APIs are on a separate authenticated channel (mTLS / mutual VPN) and cannot carry inference data.

Can we:
- Karthik: produce the one-pager diagram + 2-3 bullets about KV/cache behavior (where cache lives; whether cached prefixes are persisted to Redwood-managed storage).
- Jonas: assemble the traffic matrix (control plane, model pull, telemetry, telemetry ingest endpoints, metrics, customer inference egress) into an XLS and mark ports/egress policies.
- Marissa: quick compliance note on failover behavior (how routing/policy decides between pools/regions; our fallback to hosted variants).

Target: draft to me by 13:00 PT, final to customer by 16:00 PT. Attachments should be named clearly. I'll collate and send.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-17T12:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: short network summary + evidence for SOC2 review

Naomi — attaching drafts. See inline summary below and the two files in the Drive link.

Attachments (attached to this thread):
- network_shielding_onepager_v1.pdf (one-page diagram + key callouts)
- controlplane_egress_matrix.xlsx (traffic matrix, ports, ACL notes)
- connectivity_failover_diagram.svg (simplified failover flow)

High-level points to include in the final packet:
- Dedicated pools: customer inference traffic terminates on the Dedicated GPU pool's private subnet. There are enforced subnet-level ACLs and private routing; no public IPs are assigned to worker nodes. Management/control plane connections (orchestration, health checks) originate from a dedicated management VLAN and use mutual TLS over a customer-initiated private peering connection (for Private) or a dedicated VPN with cert-based auth for Dedicated.
- Private deployments (VPC-hosted): customer-managed VPC connects via VPC peering or Direct Connect; all inference traffic flows are kept within customer network boundaries except for optional model artifact pulls from the Redwood model store (that transfer happens over an authenticated, signed URL and can be configured to use a private mirror).
- KV/cache persistence: Inference prefix/KV caches are memory-resident on the Dedicated worker nodes by default. Optional persistent caching to Redwood-managed encrypted object storage is available but is disabled by default for Private deployments; if enabled it is written to a customer-dedicated object store bucket with SSE-KMS and restricted to the deployment's tenant scope. We call this out explicitly: no inference content is shipped to any public telemetry endpoint.
- Egress policing: All outbound control-plane egress (metrics, heartbeats) goes to specific allowlisted endpoints over TLS and is signed; customers can opt to route telemetry to their endpoints. Data classification: inference payload is treated as customer data; we do not aggregate or route inference payloads to third-party analytics without customer opt-in.
- Failover: Routing policy uses a health-check and capacity-based decision. If a Dedicated pool in us-west loses capacity or fails, we failover to the next Active/Standby pool in the same region (if configured) or route to a pinned hosted model variant with a policy that strips layer-7 headers that could include control plane metadata. Failover is logged and emitted as an audit event with timestamps.

I've added short footnotes in the PDF where we say "customer-configurable" vs "Redwood-managed". Jonas, the matrix has port-level details and suggested ACL snippets. Marissa, the failover bullets are in the last slide of the PDF — feel free to tighten language for compliance.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-openbank-evidence

-Karthik
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Subject: Network shielding and evidence pack for SOC2 (OpenBank)

Hi Linda — thanks for the call this morning. Attached is a concise pack that should meet the SOC2 reviewer ask. Brief summary below, full artifacts attached and available on Drive.

What we sent:
- network_shielding_onepager_v1.pdf — single-page diagram showing Dedicated and Private boundaries, control plane segregation, and edge egress points.
- controlplane_egress_matrix.xlsx — traffic matrix with source/destination, port/protocol, and ACL guidance.
- connectivity_failover_diagram.svg — simplified flow showing active/standby pool failover and fallback to hosted variant.

Short answers to your bullets:
- Isolation: Dedicated worker nodes have no public IPs; they live on tenant-specific subnets. Control plane uses a separate management VLAN and authenticates with mTLS/cert-based VPN.
- KV/cache: Default is in-memory on workers. Persistent cache to Redwood-managed storage is an opt-in feature; when enabled it uses per-tenant encrypted buckets (SSE-KMS) and is not shared across tenants.
- Egress: All outbound telemetry and control-plane traffic is TLS-encrypted and sent to allowlisted endpoints; customers can mirror telemetry to customer endpoints. No inference payloads are published to public telemetry services by default.
- Failover: Capacity/health-based routing within region preferred; cross-region fallback only per customer policy and with audit logging.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-openbank-evidence
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/OPENBANK-98765 (recorded packet)

If the reviewer wants a redacted packet for public filing or a diagram with callouts removed, we can produce a SOC2-ready PDF with reduced detail. Happy to jump on a short call if they want walkthrough.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Manager, Security Programs
Redwood Inference
